content.value_statement: Teams often miss review, testing, and release checks before opening pull requests. This skill provides a structured workflow for review, validation, commit planning, and PR preparation.
actual_capabilities: Coordinates code review, dependency review, and breaking change analysis.
Guides test execution, coverage review, and test gap analysis.
Creates Conventional Commit message recommendations from change context.
Plans branch strategy for trunk-based or feature-branch workflows.
Drafts pull request descriptions, metadata steps, and reviewer checklists.
limitations: It is guidance text and does not include executable scripts.
It depends on compatible subagents for review, testing, and deployment checks.
It cannot verify repository permissions without local tool access.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the reported file tree.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Review changes, plan tests, shape commits, and generate a complete PR description before publishing.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Checks
use_cases.description: Use one repeatable checklist for review quality, test coverage, branch strategy, and release readiness.

use_cases.title: Validate Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm CI expectations, security checks, rollback notes, and deployment concerns before merge.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Standard PR Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before opening a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my current branch against main. Cover code quality, tests, commit planning, and pull request description preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Draft PR Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for work in progress.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill with the draft pull request option. Identify blockers, missing tests, branch concerns, and a draft PR summary.

prompt_templates.title: Enforce Commit Standards
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced commit preparation with stricter formatting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill with Conventional Commits enforcement. Group related changes, recommend atomic commits, and call out breaking change notes.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Trunk Release Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release readiness for trunk-based teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill for a trunk-based workflow targeting main. Validate tests, branch protection, deployment readiness, rollback notes, and merge risks.

output_examples.input: Review my feature branch before I open a pull request.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow report with review findings, test status, commit recommendations, branch checks, and a pull request description outline.

output_examples.input: Prepare a release-ready PR for a risky change.
output_examples.output: A readiness summary with blocking issues, required tests, deployment notes, rollback guidance, reviewer checklist, and merge recommendations.

best_practices: Confirm the target branch, permissions, and publish policy before remote changes.
Run tests unless the team explicitly accepts the skip-tests risk.
Review generated commit messages and PR text before publication.
anti_patterns: Skipping tests for risky or user-facing changes.
Enabling auto-merge before required approvals and checks pass.
Combining unrelated work into one large pull request.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It structures a git workflow from code review through pull request preparation.

faq.question: Does it push code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and expected checks. Any repository-changing command still needs tool access and user approval.

faq.question: Can it skip tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow documents a skip-tests option, but it warns that skipping tests needs caution.

faq.question: Does it support trunk-based development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes trunk-based and feature-branch workflow modes.

faq.question: Can it help with Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides change categorization and commit message creation using the Conventional Commits format.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
